## Column vapour and cloud repair (`limiter`) {#sec-ch10-fixvapor}

After the parent-vapour borrow (@sec-ch10-borrow) a cell can still hold negative vapour, and a condensate with no
nucleation parent cannot borrow at all. Both are repaired along the column: a negative cell is grouped with the
cells below it until the group's total is non-negative. The negative cells of the group are then set to zero, and
the cells that hold vapour each give up the same fraction of it, so together they give up exactly the deficit.
The repair conserves the column's mass $\sum_i V_i\rho_{n,i}$, not its density sum, which matters on grids whose cell
volume changes with height. If nothing below can cover a deficit, the cells above supply it, bounded by the
deficit. A vapour column that cannot be repaired at all is an error; a cloud column in net deficit is clamped to
zero, which creates exactly the missing mass.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Removes negative vapour and parentless cloud along each $x_1$[^rg-431e5643024d] column, moving only the deficit; @eq-ch10-fixvapor-borrow.

**Data.** Reads and writes the species densities of interior $x_1$ columns; $V_i$[^rg-54331bf0abda] weights, $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ only tested $>0$.

**Placement.** Inside every conserved-limiter call, after the borrow; parentless cloud first, vapour second.

**Activation.** EOS `limiter: true` (default false); the split-column gather runs only for the stage-update call.

**Guarantee / limits.** Vapour: $\sum_iV_i\rho_{n,i}$ kept, an unrepairable column throws; cloud in net deficit is clamped.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch10-fixvapor-tests; `test_fix_vapor_deficit.release`, `fixvapor_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C9]`.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathcal M$ is the window of $x_1$ cells one scan step rewrites; $D$ the deficit of a window or of
the upward branch and $Q$ the vapour of a window's non-negative cells [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, per bottom-cell volume].

The repair is on with `limiter: true`.

### Derivation

Index the column from the bottom, $i=0..N-1$, with cell volumes $V_i$. The scan starts at the top. A cell with
$\rho_{n,i}\ge0$ is passed over. A negative cell starts a window $\mathcal M$ that grows downward one cell at a
time until $\sum_{l\in\mathcal M}V_l\rho_{n,l}\ge0$ or the bottom is passed. If the sum is non-negative, split the
window into its negative and its non-negative cells,

$$
D = -\sum_{l\in\mathcal M,\ \rho_{n,l}<0}\frac{V_l}{V_0}\,\rho_{n,l},\qquad
Q = \sum_{l\in\mathcal M,\ \rho_{n,l}\ge0}\frac{V_l}{V_0}\,\rho_{n,l},
$$

and rewrite every cell of the window as

$$
\rho_{n,i} \leftarrow
\begin{cases}
0, & \rho_{n,i} < 0,\\[2pt]
\rho_{n,i} - \rho_{n,i}\,\dfrac{D}{Q}, & \rho_{n,i} \ge 0,
\end{cases}
\qquad i\in\mathcal M ,
$$ {#eq-ch10-fixvapor-borrow}

and the scan resumes below the window. @eq-ch10-fixvapor-borrow is computed in `fix_vapor_impl`: the two sums are
`deficit` and `donors`, and every cell of the window is rewritten with the one fraction `share`
({{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}). The code weights by $V_l/V_0$, the volume relative to the
column's bottom cell; the factor cancels in $D/Q$. The same rule, read from the point of view of the positivity
chapter, is @eq-ch08-fixvapor-borrow.

Why the repair keeps the column mass, moves only the deficit, and terminates:

1. *The window keeps its mass.* Multiply @eq-ch10-fixvapor-borrow by $V_i/V_0$ and sum over the window. The negative
   cells give $0$ after and $-D$ before; the others give $Q - Q\,D/Q = Q - D$ after and $Q$ before. Both totals are
   $Q - D$ (`[C8]`, sympy).
2. *Every rewritten value is non-negative.* The window stopped where $Q - D \ge 0$; it holds a negative cell, so
   $D > 0$ and then $Q > 0$, and $D/Q \le 1$. Each non-negative cell keeps $(1 - D/Q)\,\rho_{n,i} \ge 0$. The code also
   guards $Q = 0$ with a share of zero ({{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}).
3. *Only the deficit moves.* The donors give up $D$ in total, each in proportion to its own vapour, and the dry
   density does not enter @eq-ch10-fixvapor-borrow; it is read only to refuse a column with $\rho_{\mathrm d}\le0$
   (`[C9]`: the same vapour column under two unrelated dry-density profiles is repaired bit for bit the same).
4. *The scan terminates.* Windows are disjoint and the scan index only decreases, so each cell is visited at most
   twice.
5. *The upward branch.* If the bottom is passed with the sum still negative, the deficit
   $D=-\sum_{l\le i_0}V_l\rho_{n,l}/V_0$ of the cells from the starting cell $i_0$ down is taken from the cells above,
   in order, each giving at most what it holds; the cells from $i_0$ down are set to zero. Before writing anything
   the branch checks that the cells above hold at least $D$, so it writes nothing when it fails
   (`deficit`, {{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}).
6. *A failure after a repaired window.* A window repaired earlier in the same scan stays rewritten: a column that
   fails below it is returned with that window borrowed from, mass kept (`[C7]`).
7. *When it fails.* The kernel fails on a non-positive dry density; otherwise, in every case `fixvapor_check.py`
   tried, only on a column whose total vapour mass is negative (`[C5]`).
8. *Round-off.* A window of $n_{\mathcal M}$ cells forms two sums of $n_{\mathcal M}$ products, one ratio, and one
   product and one difference per donor, so its mass is kept to a few $n_{\mathcal M}\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ of
   $\sum_lV_l\lvert\rho_{n,l}\rvert$; `[C4]` asserts below $10^{-13}$ relative on 1995 random columns of up to 40 cells.

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
All of this is checked against a line-for-line port of the kernel.[^fix-c] It replays the inputs of the
`eos_limiter` gtests (`[C1]`, `[C2]`, `[C3]`) and keeps $\sum_iV_i\rho_{n,i}$ below $10^{-13}$ relative on 1995
repaired random columns with unequal volumes (`[C4]`). It finds no failure on a column with non-negative total
(`[C5]`), reproduces snapy's own repair of the column of @fig-ch10-fixvapor-column to $10^{-15}$ (`[C6]`), confirms
the partial rewrite before a failure (`[C7]`) and shows that the downward branch ignores the dry density (`[C9]`).
The partial rewrite is a property of the port; it has not been reproduced in a snapy run.
:::

### Numerical method

The kernel runs once per $x_1$ column of interior cells, one CPU thread or one CUDA thread per column, inside each
call of the conserved limiter. Parentless clouds are repaired first without requiring success and then clamped;
vapour is repaired second and must succeed, `parentless`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
When the call comes from the stage update and $x_1$ is split over several blocks (`pz` > 1), every block gathers
the full column with the dry density and the volumes, repairs it and keeps its own slice
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
Failures are counted with `std::atomic` on CPU on every call
({{< code src/eos/eos_dispatch.cpp call_fix_vapor_cpu >}}). On CUDA they are counted with `atomicAdd` only when the
caller needs the count, that is when it requires success (`count`); otherwise no counter is allocated and nothing is
read. Inside a block's stage and in the floor test's conversion of `check_redo`, the vapour count is added to a 0-d
device counter of the equation of state, `vapor_failures_`, with no read
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}); `check_redo` carries it
as a seventh flag in its one device-to-host copy and raises there, and stage 0 zeroes it (@sec-ch10-redo). Any other
call reads its count back, one device synchronisation, and raises at once. A limiter call with parentless clouds runs
the kernel twice (`nerr`, {{< code src/eos/eos_dispatch.cu call_fix_vapor_cuda >}}).

After the repair, the conserved limiter marks the step for a redo only where a species density was below
$-4096\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ times the cell's total gas density before the species repairs: `species_before` against
`species_repair_mark` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}},
{{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp species_repair_mark >}}). The test reads the deficit, not how far the repair
moved the donors, so a round-off deficit next to moist air is repaired without a redo (@sec-ch10-redo,
@sec-ch08-fixvapor).

@fig-ch10-fixvapor-column shows snapy repairing a column with an interior and a bottom deficit.[^fix-run]

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-fixvapor-column
#| fig-cap: "One 64-cell spherical-polar column before and after snapy's repair, as the ratio of vapour to dry density. The vermillion dashed line with crosses is the column before, with a negative cell at index 40 and one at the bottom; the green line with dots is after. Cell 40 goes to zero and cell 39 below it gives up exactly the deficit; the bottom cell goes to zero and its deficit is taken from cell 1 above it. No other cell changes, and the column's mass is unchanged."
#| fig-alt: "Vertical profile of vapour ratio against cell index; two negative excursions before, none after."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch10.figures.fig_fixvapor_column import make_fig
```

: Code map of the column vapour and cloud repair. {#tbl-ch10-fixvapor-code}

1. Take the cell volumes so the repair conserves mass, `vol`
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
2. Gather the column when split over $x_1$ blocks, `gather_x1`
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}},
   {{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::gather_x1 >}}).
3. Run the kernel per column, `call_fix_vapor`
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
4. Throw for vapour, `require_success` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
5. Copy back this block's slice, `copy_` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
6. Mark the limiter only for a pre-repair deficit above `species_repair_mark` of the gas density, `species_before`
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).

A user can hit one message: "[EquationOfState] apply_conserved_limiter_: Failed to fix vapor mass fractions."; on
CUDA within a step it ends "(counted on the device in the step, reported at check_redo)."
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::read_redo_flags >}}).

**How to use it.** The same card as @sec-ch10-borrow: `limiter: true`. The column gather needs no key; it runs when
$x_1$ is split over blocks (`distribute/nb1` > 1) and the call comes from the stage update. The vapour call is
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}):

```cpp
    repair_column(cons.index(interior).narrow(0, ICY, nvapor), true);
```

where `true` requires success, and @eq-ch10-fixvapor-borrow is these lines of the kernel
({{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}):

```cpp
    T share = donors > 0. ? deficit / donors : T(0.);
    for (int j = is; j > i; --j) {
      vapor[j] = vapor[j] < 0. ? T(0.) : vapor[j] - vapor[j] * share;
    }
```
 Refused at run time: an unrepairable vapour column,
with "[EquationOfState] apply_conserved_limiter_: Failed to fix vapor mass fractions.", because a negative column
total cannot be made non-negative without creating mass.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_eos.release` | five `eos_limiter` columns, the borrow values exact | $10^{-14}$ rel.; 4 ulp | test thresholds |
| `test_fix_vapor_deficit.release` | only the deficit moves; the mark follows the deficit | $10^{-15}$ rel.; 4 $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ | test thresholds |
| `test_fix_vapor_volume.release` | column mass, unequal volumes | $10^{-12}$; $10^{-6}$ f32 | test thresholds |
| `test_parentless_cloud.release` | cloud kept, clamped, zero column | $10^{-12}$; $10^{-6}$ f32 | test thresholds |
| `test_vapor_column_nb1.release` | split column equals one block | bitwise | test threshold |
| `test_fix_vapor_reports_failure_python` | unrepairable column throws | n/a | message match |

: Tests of the column repair; all pass at the pin.[^fix-ctest] {#tbl-ch10-fixvapor-tests}

The `eos_limiter` cases are the inputs replayed by `fixvapor_check.py`; the bottom-cell case asserts the transfer
itself to $10^{-25}$ absolute, because a tolerance on the supplier's value would also pass a supplier that gave
nothing ({{< code tests/test_eos.cpp eos_limiter.repairs_bottom_cell_from_above >}}).
`test_fix_vapor_volume` keeps the column mass of a spherical-polar column to $10^{-12}$ in float64 and $10^{-6}$ in
float32, and on its uniform Cartesian control requires the two donors to hold the borrowed values to 4 ulp
({{< code tests/test_fix_vapor_volume.cpp DeviceTest.fix_vapor_keeps_the_column_mass_on_varying_cell_volume >}}).
`test_fix_vapor_deficit` puts $-2.5\times10^{-11}$ above a $10^{-3}$ cell and requires that cell to move by the
deficit and every other cell to keep its value bit for bit; a deficit of a quarter of the mark's bound must be
repaired without a mark ({{< code tests/test_fix_vapor_deficit.cpp eos.fix_vapor_borrows_only_the_deficit >}},
{{< code tests/test_fix_vapor_deficit.cpp eos.fix_vapor_marks_on_the_deficit >}}).
The split-column test requires every vapour cell of a two-block column to equal the one-block result exactly
({{< code tests/test_vapor_column_nb1.cpp DeviceTest.vapor_repair_keeps_the_mass_with_nb1_2 >}}).
Also registered: `test_parentless_cloud_nb1.release`, the 2-rank `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp` (rain and total
mass to $10^{-12}$), `test_fix_vapor_counts_every_column_python` (one broken column in 16384 is reported),
`test_fix_vapor_stale_count_python` (a reported failure never resurfaces in a later `check_redo`) and the CUDA
arms `test_fix_vapor_reports_failure_cuda_python` and `test_fix_vapor_stale_count_cuda_python`. Every ctest named
here that the CPU build registers passed at the pin, the two-process and Gloo arms of `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp`
included; the CUDA arms are not registered in that build and were not run.[^fix-ctest]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A vapour column whose total is negative stops the run. A cloud column whose total is negative is clamped, creating
the missing mass.
:::

- The downward branch takes the deficit from every donor of the window in proportion to its vapour, so a donor far
  below the negative cell gives as large a fraction as the one next to it. Nothing measures whether a nearest-first
  borrow would change a run.
- A failure below an already repaired window leaves that window rewritten (`fixvapor_check.py` `[C7]`, port only).
  For vapour the run stops anyway; for parentless clouds the rewrite stays, mass kept.
- When the blocks of one column live in one process, `gather_x1` waits until every one of them has posted its
  piece, so they must call the limiter concurrently; a caller that steps them one after another waits at the first
  block's gather. No registered test runs the cross-process gather on CUDA: `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp` has no
  device argument.
- The weight is relative to the bottom cell, so last-bit differences in spacing can move results at round-off.
- Not in the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix).
